verses.text: In King Hezekiah's fourteenth year, King Sennacherib of Assyria attacked every fortified city in Judah and took them.
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh and a huge army from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem. Rabshakeh stood by the water channel from the upper pool, on the road to the cloth washer's field.
Eliakim, Hilkiah's son and the man in charge of the household, came out to meet him, along with Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, Asaph's son.
Rabshakeh told them, “Tell Hezekiah this: ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says, “What are you counting on?
I say your plans and strength for battle are just empty talk. Who are you trusting enough to rebel against me?
Look at Egypt, that cracked reed you're using as a walking stick. Lean on it and it'll go straight through your hand. That's what Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is like for anyone who trusts him.
You might tell me, ‘We trust the LORD our God.’ But isn't he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah tore down when he told Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You have to worship at this altar’?”
So come on, make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I'll give you two thousand horses if you can find enough riders to put on them.
How are you supposed to turn back even one captain among the least of my master's servants? And you're counting on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
You think I came up to destroy this land without the LORD? The LORD himself told me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’”
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Please speak to us, your servants, in Aramaic. We understand it. Don't use the language of Judah with the people on the wall listening.”

Rabshakeh said, “Did my master send me with this message just for your master and you? It's for the men sitting on the wall too. They'll be eating their own dung and drinking their own urine right along with you.”
Then he stood and shouted in the language of Judah, “Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
The king says, ‘Don't let Hezekiah fool you. He can't save you.
Don't let Hezekiah talk you into trusting the LORD by saying, “The LORD will save us for sure. The king of Assyria won't get this city.”’
Don't listen to Hezekiah. The king of Assyria says, ‘Make peace with me and come out to me. Then every one of you can eat from your own vine and fig tree and drink from your own cistern,
until I come to take you to a land like yours, a land with grain and new wine, bread and vineyards.
Watch out for Hezekiah talking you into believing, “The LORD will save us.” Have any of the nations' gods saved their lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they save Samaria from me?
Which god of any of these countries saved their land from my hand? So why would the LORD save Jerusalem from my hand?’”
They stayed quiet and didn't say a word back. The king had ordered, “Don't answer him.”

Eliakim, Hilkiah's son and the man in charge of the household, came back to Hezekiah with Shebna the scribe and Joah the recorder, Asaph's son. Their clothes were torn, and they told Hezekiah what Rabshakeh had said.
